item.title: Why women should train combat sports
item.description: JadaKetley on IG. Sociologist here to back up exactly what she iterates here. Confidence and someone that looks like a hard target is a MASSIVE deterrant to public assaults. There is a caveat that there are abuses of power and gender dynamics in sports. Kinda like every other area of society. Not to minimize it at all. Social media is opening avenues for gyms that are safe for women, POC, LGBT to be visible about it and we see what gyms attract more women feeling safe there. Meta caveat that imgur usually doesn't like combat sports or violent sports. 90% of people training boxing, kickboxing, Muay Thai, jiujitsu, judo don't compete. But training it is amazing and confers social benefits. Stay safe, be strong, be kind

item.description: Donald Trump asked the FCC to punish a journalist for doubting him. Kristen Welker reported on NBC that his primary endorsement record was mixed. item.title: Cats and Memories
item.description:
Chessie slept on the towels last night, obviously worried about equitable cat hair distribution.
Later, she observed critically as dad played Cyberpunk 2077, noting that his reliance on quick hacks and stealth was unbecoming.
Frank observed Chessie observing. Later went out to dinner to celebrate the tiniest's birthday.
This connoisseur of chicken left on dad's desk on an open plate which means obviously it's fair game worked his culinary magic.
Which is to say that a chicken finger (Tysons. Previously frozen, cooked in air fryer at 390° F for 12 minutes) was reduced to this vague assembly you see before you.
Found an old journal while looking for a charger for the 3DS because the tiniest wants to play Pokémon Sun. In this journal was a face tiny octopus hadn't seen in near 25 years. And yet, a rush of memories came flooding back. Hello Ms. Taylor. I hope you're doing well and I hope that your 21st birthday was spent in a smoky bar with an array of song-inspired cocktails. Life is strange sometimes. It can be so full and rich, and you never notice until the absence makes you ache for it. That's the folly of youth, I think. I hope you all had a great weekend. And here's to those moments lost in our corner neurons that only need a slight nudge to fire up again.
